meta.title: Administrative Information Systems assessment - example report (SYNTHETIC)
meta.fiction_notice: FICTION. Northgate State University does not exist. Every finding, figure, record and locator below is invented to exercise the deck-agreement engine. Nothing here is a University of Iowa finding or a real assessment result.

evidence.source: IAM access review record, single cycle only (fictional)

findings.statement: Every sampled ESS change carries a recorded test result before release.

changes_with_recorded_test_result.basis: fictional sample of 12 changes drawn from EV-001

findings.statement: The written IAM deployment procedure requires two approvals; most sampled deployments record one.

deployments_with_single_approval.basis: fictional sample of 12 deployments drawn from EV-004

single_approval_rate_pct.basis: 7 of 12, rounded to the nearest percent

findings.statement: RIS backup jobs complete, but no restoration exercise is recorded in the assessed window, so recovery is not demonstrated.

demonstrated_recovery_time_hours.basis: no restoration exercise recorded in the assessed window; not assessed

findings.statement: Two ESS services have no recorded alert routing owner.
A quarterly IAM access review appears to run, but only one cycle's record was supplied, so this is not corroborated.

review_completion_rate_pct.basis: a single supplied cycle cannot establish a rate; not assessed

recommendations.owner_role: IAM service owner, with the change-management lead
recommendations.statement: Enforce the existing two-approval rule in the IAM deployment pipeline and record the approver pair on every deployment.

recommendations.owner_role: RIS service owner, with infrastructure operations
recommendations.statement: Run one documented restoration exercise per critical RIS dataset and record the measured recovery time.
Record a named routing owner for each ESS service alert and review the table at each service change.

recommendations.owner_role: AIS leadership, with the service owners
recommendations.statement: Extend the approval-record and restoration-evidence practice to the remaining AIS service groups once the first two phases have reported results.

roadmap.progression_note: Each phase states the evidence it is expected to produce. It does not assert a maturity level, a score, or a transformation outcome; whether practice improves is judged from the evidence the phase produces.

one_time_effort.basis: fictional estimate: pipeline change plus backfill of approver records
depends on dataset sizes and the restore target, neither of which was supplied; not assessed

recurring_effort.basis: exercise cadence not agreed; not assessed

one_time_effort.basis: fictional estimate: complete and verify the routing table

recurring_effort.basis: review cadence not agreed; not assessed

decisions.question: Do we enforce the existing two-approval rule in the IAM deployment pipeline?
options: Enforce with a documented exception path
Defer until a wider change window is sampled

decisions.question: Do we fund a documented restoration exercise for the critical RIS datasets?
options: Fund one exercise per critical dataset
Fund a single pilot dataset first
Defer until the dataset inventory is supplied

decisions.question: Who owns alert routing for the two ESS services with no recorded owner?
options: Assign to the existing service owners
Assign to the monitoring team pending service-owner confirmation
Defer to the next service review

open_inputs: Whether the fictional 12-deployment IAM sample is representative of the full change window.
Measured RIS recovery time for any critical dataset (no restoration exercise was recorded).
The second IAM access-review cycle record needed to corroborate F-005.
Restoration effort and cadence for RES-002, and the alert-review cadence for RES-003.
